projects.name: archctl
projects.summary: Architecture linter and VS Code extension for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Java.
implemented: AST-based scanners build dependency graphs and detect module imports and side-effect capabilities.
Nine rule implementations enforce allowed/forbidden layers and capabilities, context visibility, cycles, external dependencies, file placement, and dependency limits.
Clean Architecture, DDD microservices, and modular monolith templates; interactive init and rule/context/layer management.
Incremental scan cache invalidates on file/config/tsconfig changes.
Text/JSON/interactive HTML reports with architecture health/dependency graph/layer matrix.
VS Code file watcher reruns checks and maps results into inline diagnostics.
Baseline/ratchet/trend features exist but were substantially authored by contributor Raymond.

attribution.note: Counts from GitHub contributors; not effort or ownership percentages. Debt tracking PR #20 by RaymondC-tech/raymond367; Ethan reviewed/merged.

not_verified: Marketplace publication of VS Code extension; source version is 0.2.0.
Performance speedup, active users, package downloads.
conflicts: CHANGELOG dates list 2024/Jan2025, a year before repo creation and npm releases; use API/npm timestamps.
sync and prompt commands are stubs: no documentation-sync or architecture-aware prompt-generation claim.
draft_bullets: Built and published an architecture linter for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Java, with nine rules for dependency boundaries, side effects, and circular imports.
Added a VS Code extension, cached code scans, and interactive dependency reports so architecture violations show up while you work.

projects.name: Cybermetrics
projects.summary: Baseball roster analysis using team-relative z-scores and replacement simulation across five offensive metrics.
implemented: React/TypeScript roster and lineup builders, player search, radar charts, recommendations.
FastAPI with Firebase auth/Firestore and pybaseball data; routes/services/domain/repository separation.
Recommendation service identifies weakest player, simulates same-position replacements, ranks reduction in roster weakness.
Player cache reuse, singleton dependency injection, startup cache preload.
Pytest unit/integration suites and Vitest client action tests wired into GitHub Actions.

attribution.note: Avoid presenting entire analytics algorithm as solely Ethan’s invention; primary authored PRs support engineering/testing/caching ownership.

reported_metrics.claim: ~364 to ~2 Firestore reads per recommendation, ~99.5% reduction
reported_metrics.evidence: Ethan-authored merged PR #164, explicit before/after modeled workload; source implements cache reuse
reported_metrics.classification: PR-reported workload estimate, not independently benchmarked
PR-reported historical test result; no fresh run. PR subcounts 486+40+23 do not equal 509, so omit breakdown.

draft_bullets: Built roster analysis and recommendation flows in React and FastAPI, helping users find players who address their lineup’s specific weaknesses.
Cut Firestore reads from roughly 364 to 2 per recommendation by reusing a shared player cache.
Expanded backend test coverage from 37.76% to 92.77% and added 49 frontend action tests.
projects.copy_note: Second and third bullets use historical PR-reported metrics; suitable after user confirms they reflect their measured results. Do not imply current live benchmark.

projects.name: now
projects.summary: Scheduled activity collection produces static Markdown and JSON for humans and agents.

Historical writing tool file exists but stale and not currently in main snapshot.
Contribution counts include automated activity; not quality/productivity metric.
draft_bullets: Built a self-updating status page and JSON API that derives current projects and activity from GitHub and WakaTime on an hourly schedule.
Served committed snapshots through Vercel’s edge cache, with last-good-data fallbacks when upstream APIs fail.
